items.title: Built a desktop app in a single day using Opus 5.5 that bridges Hermes and Slack, and it’s mind-blow...
items.content:
Built a desktop app in a single day using Opus 5.5 that bridges Hermes and Slack, and it’s mind-blowing.

It syncs with a remote Mac mini bot, and whenever I reply, Slack picks it up instantly while Hermes briefs me right here on the desktop with, "Here's what came in."

You can switch models on the fly, the UI is super clean, and it even fixes that annoying Slack issue where approval requests get lost in threads or stuck in infinite waiting loops 

it pushes notifications and lets you check everything at a glance on the main dashboard.

Honestly, this is insane. At this point, building your own custom desktop app is just way better than using existing ones. It turned out ridiculously well.

this project is not open-source but i used it >> https://t.co/g1exHwWK5E

items.title:
How to 100% Guarantee Open-Source Success

1. Start with something YOU desperately want to get good ...
items.content:
How to 100% Guarantee Open-Source Success

1. Start with something YOU desperately want to get good at. (If you're starting with something others desperately want, go start a business instead—what the hell are you doing in open source?)
2. Look down on everyone else's inefficient garbage and make yours insanely better.
3. Build things that others COULD build, but are too lazy to actually do. And make it look fucking pretty—this part is crucial.
4. Spam the absolute hell out of X (Twitter). Farm engagement, draw attention, and post tons of slick, pretty visuals.
5. Wake up one day and realize you've made it. (Results may vary for actual businesses.)
